profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer at WP Engine
profile.summary: Full-stack software architect, with over 25 years of experience delivering mission-critical software applications for a variety of markets. Pragmatic and results-oriented professional with a passion for the craft of creating great software.  Proven track record of strong communication skills and the ability to work with a wide variety of individuals across and outside an organization.

positions.title: Architect
positions.description:
As Solutions Architect for the BMC Performance Manager (BPM), defined the product strategy and designed the architecture to implement that strategy. Implemented agile development techniques (Scrum) and assisted in implementation of three releases in 2005. Collaborates with both Product Marketing and Development to define and clarify use-cases and requirements within the agile team. Successfully coordinates with project members across the continent and around the world.

As a developer and technical lead, worked on a variety of products within the PATROL ® product family (PATROL Agent, PATROL Central console, PATROL for UNIX Knowledge Module, PATROL Knowledge Module Deployment Server, and PATROL Console Integration Toolkit). PATROL ® is a leading enterprise systems management product, which pioneered the use of autonomous agents to monitor critical system resources and applications. These products span the range from customer-facing solutions, to internal infrastructure to software development kits.

positions.title: Application Developer
positions.description: Provided clients with application engineering services to extend and maintain an X-Windows based framework for real-time, command-control GUI development. Clients included a variety of petrochemical, process control and aerospace companies including NASA, Lockheed Martin, Siemens and ARCO.

company.name: Kinesix, a division of Scientific Software Intercomp

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Programmed the full range of company products encompassing DOS, Macintosh, VMS, and UNIX Systems for newspaper publishing applications based on a client/server architecture linking DOS and Macintosh user workstations with UNIX and VMS database fileservers using TCP/IP sockets.
